title: Greeting Prefix: Thrashing to Stability
description: Many rapid attempts with oscillation before converging to a correct final solution.
why_interesting: Shows high-effort thrashing behavior that eventually self-corrects, useful for discussing process quality vs effort.

timeline.text: Task: detect whether input starts with a greeting prefix. The student starts with runtime failures.
Even after many runs, still runtime-heavy. They may be “trying one more edit” without a stable debugging checkpoint.
First all-public pass appears. This often creates confidence, but private validation is the real gate.
Private score drops to partial (67). Hidden inputs likely violate a string-handling assumption.
Regression phase: public correctness slips again. This is a hallmark of volatile code changes.
Private all-pass arrives. The student finally aligns the logic for both visible and hidden cases.
First successful submission lands. The core problem is solved and verified.
Repeat successful submission confirms stability. Good clip for discussing “thrashing can still recover, but at high cost.”
